text: Two independent sources corroborate the tree-cover loss in 2021. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) detects 81.3 ha of loss in 2021, confirmed by later years in the series. The JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset agrees that 98% of the event area was forested in 2020, meeting the 50% threshold for corroboration. Additionally, Uruguay’s national forest cartography (MGAP 2021) classifies the affected area as planted forest (68.1 ha of *Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*), with no native forest present. While 37.3 ha of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 ha (excluded from the event count), the remaining area aligns with the corroborated loss.
